The AI bot ruleset identifies AI bots, groups them by purpose, and enforces your choice for each group at the edge. items.description: Azure Backup now supports cross-subscription backup for Azure Virtual Machines, enabling customers to protect VMs using a Recovery Services vault located in a different Azure subscription within the same tenant. This capability allows organizations to centralize backup management across multiple subscriptions, simplifying backup administration, improving governance, and reducing the need to maintain separate backup vaults in each subscription. items.description: Azure Boost observability for NVMe disks is an open-source command-line tool that you run inside compatible Azure VMs. Backed by Azure Boost, the tool provides remote disk I/O and latency metrics and maps each disk inside your VM to the corresponding disk shown in the Azure portal. This helps you investigate remote disk performance and associate metrics with the right disk. Learn more.

items.description: Immutable snapshots for Azure Disk Storage are now available in public preview. You can now apply an immutability policy to snapshots of any Azure disk type to prevent deletion for up to 90 days. While the policy is active, no one can delete the snapshot, regardless of role or permissions. This helps protect backups from ransomware, meet regulatory requirements for short-term backups that need fast restore, and guard against rogue AI agent behavior. items.title: Generally Available: Intel and AMD v6 with temp disk for Azure Database for PostgreSQL
items.description: Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server is announcing the general availability of Intel and AMD v6 compute tiers with local temporary disk. The new v6 generation expands the Flexible Server compute portfolio with higher performance, larger scale, and improved price/performance while retaining local temporary disk for workloads that benefit from it. You can select the latest v6 Intel and AMD compute options based on your workload requirements while continuing to use the familiar PostgreSQL Flexible Server experience. Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Intel and AMD v5 diskless tier for Azure Database for PostgreSQL
items.description: Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server is announcing the general availability of Intel and AMD V5 diskless compute. These new options expand the v5 compute portfolio with General Purpose and Memory Optimized SKUs that do not include local temporary SSD. If your workloads don’t require local temporary storage, you can select these diskless v5 configurations while retaining the PostgreSQL Flexible Server experience. The new options include Intel and AMD-based compute families across General Purpose and Memory Optimized tiers. Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Cobalt 200 compute for Azure Database for PostgreSQL
items.description: Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server is announcing the general availability of Cobalt 200 ARM-based compute. Cobalt 200 expands the Flexible Server compute portfolio with Microsoft-designed ARM64-based compute, giving you an additional architecture choice alongside Intel and AMD x64-based compute. With Cobalt 200, you can choose the compute architecture that best fits your PostgreSQL workload, compatibility, and infrastructure requirements. Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Geo-redundant backup and restore for Azure HorizonDB
items.description: Geo-redundant backup and restore for Azure HorizonDB is now available. You can use geo-redundant backups to strengthen data protection and restore your HorizonDB deployment in another Azure region when needed. With this capability, you have an additional recovery option for scenarios that require cross-region recovery, helping you improve business continuity and disaster recovery preparedness. Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Customize backup retention from 1 to 35 days in Azure HorizonDB
items.description: You can now configure backup retention for your Azure HorizonDB deployments from 1 to 35 days, giving you greater flexibility to align backup retention with your application and data protection requirements. Choose the retention period that best fits your workload and recovery needs while Azure HorizonDB manages backups for you. Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Throughput buckets in Azure Cosmos DB
items.description: We're excited to announce the general availability of throughput buckets in Azure Cosmos DB. You can manage the resource consumption of multiple workloads using the same container by limiting the maximum throughput a workload can consume. You may need to manage workload throughput consumption in scenarios like: Multitenant workloads managed by Independent Software Vendors (ISVs). Bulk execution in ETL jobs. Data ingestion and migration processes. Change feed processing. You can create throughput buckets in a Cosmos DB container using Data Explorer in the Azure portal. Learn more.

items.description: AI model management in Azure HorizonDB is now in limited preview, designed to simplify how you bring AI into your database. items.title: Generally Available: Semantic Reranker in Azure Cosmos DB
items.description: Semantic Reranker in Azure Cosmos DB improves search relevance by reordering candidate results based on the meaning of the search text and surrounding context. It uses an AI model to evaluate candidate documents and promote the ones that best match the intent of a query or natural language question, helping you deliver more accurate, context-aware answers in search and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) scenarios. items.description: Isolated pods should not force a tradeoff between security and startup performance. With classic sandboxed pod flows, every pod boots a new Kata VM, which adds cold-start latency and extra memory overhead before your app begins work. The new kata-vm-isolation-v2 runtime class changes that default. It creates pods from a pre-initialized sandbox VM template instead of booting each sandbox from scratch, reduces per-pod memory overhead, and uses Kata’s Rust runtime for better efficiency. items.description: Azure Elastic SAN Next Generation is now in public preview. Elastic SAN Next Generation keeps the core benefits customers value in Elastic SAN today: a single SAN resource hierarchy to consolidate block storage workloads and dynamically share performance, simplifying storage management and lowering total cost of ownership at scale. items.title: Public Preview: Database Agent for SQL with contextual Copilot
items.description: Database Agent now gives you AI-generated, evidence-grounded recommendations for detected database issues, including why the issue matters, the likely cause, and the recommended next step. Recommendations draw on available issue evidence and Microsoft-authored scenario knowledge. They distinguish observed evidence from AI-generated conclusions and communicate uncertainty when evidence is incomplete, stale, or conflicting. Recommendations are presented for your review before any state-changing action. Learn more.

items.description: Database Hub in Microsoft Fabric gives you built-in, real-time performance dashboards for Microsoft SQL, Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server, and Azure Cosmos DB in one place. items.description: Foundry IQ supported Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers as federated knowledge sources, is generally available. Customers register an MCP server as a read-only knowledge source in Foundry IQ. MCP knowledge sources participate in Foundry IQ cross-source selection alongside other knowledge sources, such as web search and unstructured data in blob storage synced into Azure AI Search vector indexes. Learn more.

items.description: The Azure Content Understanding skill in Azure AI Search is generally available for semantic chunking and AI-generated image descriptions, for use with Foundry IQ and Azure AI Search. The skill produces semantically coherent chunks with structured Markdown, location metadata, and searchable image descriptions in an Azure AI Search enrichment pipeline. Learn more.

items.description: Azure Backup now supports snapshot-based backup for SQL Server running on Azure Virtual Machines. This new capability uses Azure disk snapshots combined with native SQL transaction log backups to deliver near-instant, low-impact full backups for large SQL databases, significantly improving backup performance and reducing the load on production workloads compared to streaming backups. items.title: Public Preview: Confidential VMs with OS Disk Encryption support on AKS
items.description: Regulated customers running AKS Confidential VM node pools protect workloads in memory today, but the OS disk isn't encrypted at rest, so they have to close the data-at-rest gap outside the platform. In Preview, Ubuntu 26.04 Confidential VM node pools enable OS Disk Encryption by default on both Intel TDX and AMD SEV-SNP SKUs, so the OS disk is protected with a CVM-bound key from first boot. Confidential workloads get end-to-end confidentiality (memory and OS disk) without new configuration, new API surface, or changes to existing tooling. Learn more.

items.description: Customers standardized on Intel Trust Domain Extensions (TDX) for attestation and hardware confidentiality can't run those workloads on AKS Confidential VM node pools today, because CVM node images only support AMD SEV-SNP. AKS Confidential VM node pools add Intel TDX support alongside AMD SEV-SNP, and the correct CVM image is selected automatically from the VM SKU. items.title: Generally Available: Private endpoint support for Azure HorizonDB clusters
items.description: You can now connect to Azure HorizonDB clusters privately through Azure Private Link, using a private IP address from your virtual network. Private DNS integration makes connection setup easier, while the option to disable public access keeps database traffic off the public internet. Connections are supported from: Azure virtual networks. Peered networks. On-premises environments through VPN or Azure ExpressRoute. Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Service tags for inbound rules in network security perimeter
items.description: Announcing the public preview of 'service tags as inbound rules' support for third-party customers in network security perimeter. items.description: This capability enables secure connectivity between resources protected by different network security perimeters, while maintaining strong perimeter-based access controls. Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: User-assigned managed identity for Azure HorizonDB
items.description: User-assigned managed identity (UMI) support is now generally available for Azure HorizonDB, enabling you to assign and centrally manage Azure identities for your HorizonDB clusters. With UMI, you can reduce the need to manage credentials for secure access to Azure resources. You can use UMIs with supported HorizonDB capabilities, including customer-managed keys (CMK) and Microsoft Entra authentication, helping you build more secure integrations while reducing the operational burden of managing credentials. Learn more.

items.description: Microsoft Entra authentication is now generally available for Azure HorizonDB, providing a more secure, identity-based approach to database authentication. You can use Microsoft Entra authentication to centrally manage identities and access instead of relying solely on locally managed database passwords, helping you reduce credential-management overhead and strengthen your security posture. items.title: Public Preview: Azure Database for MySQL on Premium SSD v2
items.description: Azure Database for MySQL now supports Premium SSD v2 (managed disks) in public preview. Premium SSD v2 provides higher performance and better price-performance compared to Premium File Share, with the flexibility to independently scale storage capacity, IOPS, and throughput. This update enables you to optimize costs and performance based on your workload requirements, from steady-state applications to bursty, transaction-intensive workloads. Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Cosmos DB full-text search BM25 score projection
items.description: Azure Cosmos DB full-text search now includes BM25 score projection, giving you clear visibility into why results appear in the order they do. Your app can now access the relevance score for each result directly, making search ranking more transparent. This new capability helps you display relevance, troubleshoot unexpected ordering, and tune ranking with confidence. You can also compare how different ranking signals contribute to final relevance, helping you build better search experiences on top of your Azure Cosmos DB data. Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Managed Redis database integration guidance
items.description: Improved database integration guidance for Azure Managed Redis helps you add caching to applications built with Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server, Azure Cosmos DB, and Azure SQL. You can use practical guidance, reference architectures, and step-by-step tutorials to implement caching best practices and common patterns. These resources help you reduce database load, improve application responsiveness, and choose the right caching approach for your workload. Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Managed Redis keyspace notifications
items.description: Keyspace notifications are now generally available for Azure Managed Redis, enabling your applications to receive events through pub/sub when data in your cache changes. You can configure the event types that matter to your application and subscribe to notifications for selected keys or operations. These notifications help you build event-driven applications that monitor key changes, respond to expirations, and trigger downstream actions without continuously polling the cache. You can update the notification settings as your application requirements evolve. Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Managed Redis agent kit

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Cache for Redis to Azure Managed Redis migration tooling
items.description: The general availability of built-in DNS migration tooling simplifies endpoint migration from Azure Cache for Redis Basic, Standard, and Premium tiers to Azure Managed Redis. The tooling lets you redirect the existing cache hostname to an existing Azure Managed Redis instance, allowing applications to reconnect using the same hostname and access key. The tool also supports data retention across migration. This built-in tooling reduces immediate application configuration changes and simplifies traffic cutover while you validate the new cache. items.title: Public Preview: IP filtering in Azure Managed Redis

items.description: Azure Managed Redis now provides shard-level metrics, giving you greater visibility into the performance of individual shards. This update helps you protect applications against zonal failures while retaining the performance, scalability, and price-performance benefits of Next-gen General Purpose. Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Backup for Azure Cosmos DB
items.description: Vaulted backups add an independent protection layer by storing immutable backup copies in an Azure Backup vault, isolated from the source Azure Cosmos DB account, and managed through Azure Backup. items.title: Public Preview: Embedding generation in Azure Cosmos DB
items.description: Embedding generation converts content into vector embeddings that capture semantic meaning, helping applications find relevant information beyond exact keyword matches. It uses specialized Azure Data-developed models to support semantic search and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). With the Azure.Data.AI SDK, you can add embedding generation directly to retrieval workflows for RAG and agent applications through a focused interface. Learn more.

items.description: The Azure Cosmos DB SDK for Rust gives you a native Rust client for building applications on Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL. You get access to database operations directly from Rust, with built-in performance optimizations and failure handling. Efficient binary encoding, automatic retries, and partition-level failover and circuit breaking are enabled by default. These capabilities help you build reliable, high-performance applications with less client configuration and custom recovery logic. Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Full-text search in Azure DocumentDB

With support for additional data types and the compound operator for filtering, you can build more expressive search queries over your document data. These capabilities give you greater control over which results are returned and how they are ranked, without deploying a separate search service. Learn more.
